## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `federated-relevance-calibration`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-07-25T17:55:26.153Z.

Algorithm (23) federated relevance calibration and cross-workspace budget allocation — extending the catalog 2026-07-25.

Gap this closes: algorithms (1)-(22) all assume a single workspace. Activation (1) is measured in that workspace's access rate, learned weights (3) are fit on its labels, sketches (8) summarize its history, and the shrinkage prior (21) pools within it. Federation (pm-odohgb, story pm-is1a) makes N workspaces addressable in one context assembly, and at that point every existing signal becomes incomparable across sources: a three-item scratch repo and a decade-old monolith produce activation values that differ by orders of magnitude for work of identical relevance. A naive merge lets the busiest workspace flood the budget, which is the failure mode an organization notices immediately.

Method, in three parts:

1. Rank-normalize within source before any cross-source comparison. Convert each source's candidate scores to within-source quantiles, then fuse. This is the same insight that makes (5) reciprocal rank fusion the right cold-start combiner — rank is robust exactly where magnitude is not — applied one level up, from signals-within-a-workspace to workspaces-within-a-federation.

2. Treat the token budget as an allocation across sources rather than a single pool. Each source receives budget proportional to its expected marginal value per token, estimated with the same submodular measure as (4), but with the redundancy penalty computed across sources as well as within them — an item mirrored or referenced in two federated workspaces must be paid for once. Sources with no local usage history back off to a federation-level shrinkage prior (21), so a newly joined workspace inherits the fleet's prior instead of a flat default and does not need a cold-start special case.

3. Decay by sync lag, not wall clock. A remote workspace last synchronized three weeks ago has a recency distribution frozen at the sync point; scoring its items on wall-clock recency makes stale remotes look artificially hot. Activation from a remote source decays against its own last-sync watermark, and the watermark travels with the federated reference.

Degeneracy requirement, per the catalog's standing rule: with one source the allocation reduces to (4) exactly and the normalization is the identity, so a single-workspace user pays nothing for federation-awareness.

Owner: transport and addressing belong to pm-odohgb; the scoring changes land in the pm-h3no scorer contract once federated sources exist. Recorded on pm-g8t7b9.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
